_readme: Cross-language conformance fixture for the listen-address merge rule.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the hub folds a covered listen address into the address
that covers it, because a wildcard bind already answers on every address of its
family -- so binding `*:4327` beside `127.0.0.1:4327` fails with EADDRINUSE
rather than serving both. internal/hub/listenset owns that rule and is the
enforcement point. The Network access panel MIRRORS it, to tell the operator
before Apply which of the addresses they typed will disappear into another one;
without the preview, an address they asked for is simply absent from 'Serving
now' a second later and reads as one the hub dropped.
A mirror nobody checks silently stops matching, and here that means a preview
that promises one thing and a hub that does another. This file is that check:
both suites read it, so EDITING ONE SIDE WITHOUT THE OTHER IS THE EXACT BUG IT
PREVENTS -- the language that drifts is the one whose CI turns red.
CONSUMED BY (keep both in sync with this schema):
Go: backend/internal/hub/listenset/listenset_test.go  TestCovers_Conformance
TS: frontend/src/components/settings/controls/networkAddress.test.ts
THE CONTRACT, per case: `a` covers `b` iff `covers`. Both sides assert their own
spelling of that one sentence:
Go asserts  listenset.MustParse(a).Covers(listenset.MustParse(b)) == covers
TS asserts  covers(parseAddress(a), parseAddress(b)) === covers
Covers is deliberately INCOMPLETE in one place, and the cases say so: on a host
with net.ipv6.bindv6only=0, `[::]` takes the IPv4 stack as well, so `[::]:4327`
and `192.168.1.24:4327` collide although neither covers the other here. A sysctl
is not readable from an address, so neither side folds that pair; the bind fails
with EADDRINUSE and the caller reports it.
